g1|variants|listing and exclusion.family_title: Product Listing and Exclusion Family in SAP S/4HANA OTC
g1|variants|listing and exclusion.summary: Product listing and exclusion controls which materials a customer is allowed to buy or is strictly blocked from purchasing during sales order entry. The variants differ by whether the system performs an inclusion check (listing) or an exclusion check (exclusion), and whether the master data is maintained as condition records or via customer/material assortments.

variants.name: Standard Product Listing (Inclusion)
variants.when_used: When specific customers are restricted to purchase only an approved subset of products.
variants.key_config: Define listing procedure, assign to sales document type, and maintain condition records via VB01.

variants.name: Standard Product Exclusion
variants.when_used: When specific customers are strictly prohibited from ordering certain dangerous or restricted products.
variants.key_config: Define exclusion procedure, assign to sales document type, and maintain exclusion records via VB51.

variants.name: Listing via Product Proposal / Assortment
variants.when_used: Retail or wholesale scenarios where customer assortments dynamically drive material availability.
variants.key_config: Configure retail assortment modules, link to customer hierarchy, and activate listing check in sales area.

variants.name: Exclusion via Material Status Check
variants.when_used: Blocking discontinued or blocked-for-sale materials from being added to any sales order.
variants.key_config: Maintain material status in material master (MM02) and configure sales status checks in SD control.

g1|core|listing and exclusion|standard p.title: Standard Product Listing (Inclusion)
g1|core|listing and exclusion|standard p.story: Just like a VIP club only lets in people with a special golden ticket, this feature makes sure customers can only order specific products that are allowed for them. In technical terms, the system evaluates condition technique during sales document entry to check whether a material is allowed for a customer based on validity periods and customer-material relationships.
g1|core|listing and exclusion|standard p.why_business_needs_it: This setup prevents costly fulfillment errors and contract breaches by automatically blocking unauthorized items from being ordered by specific customers. It enforces commercial agreements, regional product restrictions, and promotional assortments directly at order entry.

g1|core|listing and exclusion|standard p.title: Standard Product Exclusion
g1|core|listing and exclusion|standard p.story: Imagine a store owner who blocks specific candy bars from being sold to a certain customer because of an allergy warning, ensuring the cash register automatically stops the cashier from ringing them up. In SAP S/4HANA Sales and Distribution (SD), Product Exclusion prevents unauthorized or restricted materials from being ordered by specific customers or distribution channels during order entry. When a sales employee attempts to add an excluded material to a sales order, the system intercepts the entry and triggers a hard rejection or warning based on condition technique configurations. This ensures compliance with regional regulations, contract agreements, or stock allocation restrictions before orders reach outbound delivery and billing.
g1|core|listing and exclusion|standard p.why_business_needs_it: The business enforces product exclusion to prevent legal liabilities, avoid costly order cancellations due to embargoed or restricted items, and automate compliance with contractual agreements. Without this automated control, customer service representatives could inadvertently accept orders for restricted items, leading to manual rework, delivery blocks, and customer dissatisfaction.

g1|core|listing and exclusion|listing vi.title: Listing via Product Proposal / Assortment
g1|core|listing and exclusion|listing vi.story:
Imagine a store owner who only wants to offer certain summer toys on shelves during June, so the cash register automatically blocks any other toy from being sold. In SAP S/4HANA Sales and Distribution (SD), listing via product proposal and assortment uses condition technique to restrict which materials customers can order based on assigned assortment modules. When a sales order is created, the system checks the listing procedure against the customer and material master to ensure the transaction is permitted.

Technically, listing and exclusion uses condition tables, access sequences, and condition types assigned to a listing procedure. The procedure is linked to the sales document type and customer master data to control valid material selection during order entry.
g1|core|listing and exclusion|listing vi.why_business_needs_it: This mechanism prevents order entry errors by restricting sales representatives from selling unauthorized or discontinued products to specific customers. It enforces contractual agreements, regional sales rights, and promotional assortments directly at the Order-to-Cash (OTC) entry point.

modules.role: Owns the listing procedure, condition records, sales document types, and blocks unauthorized sales orders during OTC processing.
modules.hands_off_to: FI-AR (Financial Accounting - Accounts Receivable) and LE-SHP (Logistics Execution - Shipping) upon successful order creation and subsequent delivery and billing.

modules.role: Maintains material master views and product hierarchy data that serve as the foundation for assortment modules and condition record assignment.
modules.hands_off_to: SD (Sales and Distribution) for material validation during order processing.

prerequisites: Organizational structure (Sales Organization, Distribution Channel, Division) fully configured via OVX5 and VOR1.
Customer Master Records created with assigned listing procedures via XD01 or BP.

g1|panel|listing and exclusion.otc_impact: Listing and exclusion control which materials customers can order, acting as an automated gatekeeper at the sales order entry point in Order-to-Cash. By enforcing these rules via condition technique or material master status, it prevents invalid orders, reduces downstream delivery rejects, and ensures compliance with commercial agreements and regional regulations before billing and cash collection.

panel_qa.question: How do we handle a critical global customer who urgently needs an excluded product without redesigning our entire assortment hierarchy?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Listing and exclusion operate on condition technique via application V (Sales/Distribution) using condition tables like A001 for customer/material. When an urgent exception arises, the correct governance path is not disabling the exclusion procedure globally, but rather granting temporary authorization via a specific user role or creating a manual exception record with a defined validity period in transaction VKH1. This preserves auditability and prevents system bypasses while unblocking revenue. From a leadership perspective, this balances rigorous compliance with operational agility, maintaining order accuracy KPIs without introducing compliance risks. Next, we should review if this exception signals a broader market demand that warrants a permanent assortment revision in SAP Product Lifecycle Management. Trap: The weak approach is disabling the material exclusion procedure entirely for the user or sales area.
panel_qa.trap: Disabling the material exclusion procedure entirely for the user or sales area to push the order through.

panel_qa.question: Why use condition-based listing and exclusion over material master status checks, and what is the total cost of maintenance for each approach?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Condition-based listing using condition tables and access sequences in pricing/listing allows granular control per customer, customer hierarchy, or sales area with time-bound validity periods. Conversely, material master status checks via field MVKE-VMSTA apply a hard stop globally or per sales area, independent of specific customer tiers. Condition records offer high commercial flexibility but create master data overhead, whereas material status checks are ideal for phase-out products like discontinued lines. Financially, choosing the wrong approach leads to bloated maintenance costs or manual order entry errors that delay cash collection. Next, we standardize our product launch framework to mandate material status checks for lifecycle phases and condition records strictly for commercial customer-specific assortments. Trap: Using complex condition records for simple product obsolescence management.
panel_qa.trap: Using complex condition records for simple product obsolescence management instead of leveraging material status checks.

panel_qa.question: How does the listing and exclusion engine integrate with external B2B portals or CPQ systems to prevent invalid items from reaching SAP S/4HANA?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: External systems such as SAP Commerce Cloud or CPQ must replicate or query the listing and exclusion logic to ensure customers do not build carts with unorderable items. In an integrated architecture, the external system calls SAP APIs or SD synchronous order simulation functions like BAPI_SALESORDER_SIMULATE, which evaluate the listing procedure assigned in customer master data (table KNVV-AWAIS). If a material is excluded, the API returns error message V1 302 (Material &1 is not listed for customer &2). This prevents failed IDocs or blocked orders in S/4HANA and protects order-to-cash cycle time metrics. Next, we will audit our API payload mappings to guarantee that listing check error messages are clearly surfaced in the customer-facing UI. Trap: Relying entirely on batch IDoc error handling in SAP after the invalid order has already been submitted by the customer.
panel_qa.trap: Relying entirely on batch IDoc error handling in SAP after the invalid order has already been submitted by the customer.

panel_qa.question: What happens to open sales orders when a new product exclusion rule is activated in production?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Activation of a new exclusion condition record does not automatically invalidate or re-price existing open sales orders already present in table VBAK/VBAP. The listing and exclusion check is fundamentally an order-creation-time control governed by transaction VOV8 (Sales Document Type) and procedure assignment. If an order is already open, subsequent changes like quantity updates may trigger a re-determination depending on copy control settings in VTLA or VTAF. From a risk perspective, failing to understand this means excluded items could still ship and bill unless a mass re-determination or manual review is enforced. Next, we implement a periodic scheduling job using SD report RVV05V02 to check open orders against newly modified master data. Trap: Assuming that creating an exclusion record instantly cancels or blocks all existing open orders for that material.
panel_qa.trap: Assuming that creating an exclusion record instantly cancels or blocks all existing open orders for that material.

panel_qa.question: How do we ensure that business users maintain listings efficiently during mass product launches without creating conflicting condition records?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Mass maintenance of listing condition records must be executed via transaction LSMW, SAP Information Lifecycle Management, or SAP Fiori app 'Manage Price Sales Conditions' using standard condition tables like A003. To avoid overlapping validity periods and performance degradation during order entry, we enforce strict exclusion procedures in Customizing (SPRO > Sales and Distribution > Basic Functions > Listing and Exclusion). Leadership value is achieved by eliminating manual data entry errors, which directly safeguards the On-Time In-Full (OTIF) delivery metric and avoids revenue leakage. Next, we will establish governance workflows via SAP Master Data Governance (MDG) for customer assortments. panel_qa.question: What is the financial and operational impact on the cash conversion cycle if material status checks are misconfigured during a product recall?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: During a product recall, setting the material status in field MVKE-VMSTA (Sales Status) to block both orders and deliveries ensures immediate risk mitigation. If misconfigured—such as blocking orders but leaving deliveries active—open orders created prior to the recall can still generate outbound delivery documents and billing documents, resulting in severe regulatory liabilities and credit memos. Financially, this creates disputed invoices and delayed cash collection due to customer returns. Next, we map all recall scenarios directly to automated status updates that halt the entire order-to-cash pipeline from sales order creation down to billing. Trap: Setting the message type in delivery settings to warning instead of error for discontinued or recalled materials.

g1|core|listing and exclusion|exclusion.story: Imagine a giant candy store that is not allowed to sell certain candies to kids in specific states because of local rules, so the cash register automatically hides those candies from the screen when that state is chosen. g1|core|listing and exclusion|exclusion.why_business_needs_it: Organizations must comply with regional regulations, contractual restrictions, and phased product lifecycles by preventing unauthorized or discontinued items from being ordered.
